classification: Automated fictional standalone WordPress rehearsal; captured mail, no real delivery or human usability evidence

host_move.kind: Replacement service instances and restored directories on one workstation, same issuer; not a physical host, DNS, Pubky or independent-operator migration

checks: A separately signed-in organisation admin approves the fictional member through the form.
Real WordPress setup selects v1 scopes, pins the operator key, recognises the organisation and uses the host name for member sign-in.
Email-code login creates a Subscriber without shared email; PHP verifies and accepts the selected organisation membership.
A restored replacement installation keeps issuer, keys, accounts, approvals, sharing choices and the working private WordPress page; a changed issuer is refused.
A new WordPress login after replacement reuses the same account and starts with the saved name, membership and confirmation choices.
Revocation removes membership access on the next request without deleting the WordPress account; reapproval restores current evidence.
WordPress renews the v1 server-side session without another member login.
Withholding membership removes access even though organisation approval remains active.
Explicit linking preserves the existing WordPress account and email without creating a duplicate.
Issuer outage blocks connected access, preserves native admin login, and recovers.
Disconnect ends only that connection and revokes its refresh token.
A second restore preserves the disconnection and rejected refresh token while the other member keeps access to their account.
A sign-in URL copied to another browser cannot create a WordPress session.
